channel.title: Daily Recap — 🚦Start Up
channel.description: What happened in 🚦Start Up, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
item.description:
Less than two weeks after ousting him, Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a stunning reversal backed by senior U.S. government officials. President Trump said he called into the board meeting to advocate for Huang's return and publicly endorsed the decision, saying the U.S. has no evidence of wrongdoing and citing the attorney general, while urging Nvidia to continue its export-control investigation. Employees greeted Huang like a hero at headquarters, where he told them he would be “a better CEO the second time around.”

The scandal is far from over. The Wall Street Journal reports Huang disclosed additional affairs beyond the two already reported during his Sunday meeting with the board. Megaspeed, the company at the center of the affair allegations and previously led by Alice Huang, appears headed for a U.S. blacklist that would bar it from doing business with American companies. Politicians on both sides of the aisle reacted with anger, and Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate next week about the affair with the suspected Chinese spy.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
  • Techmeme: Sources: Jensen Huang disclosed additional affairs beyond the two already reported during his Sunday meeting with Nvidia's board, but was remorseful about them (Wall Street Journal)

  • TechCrunch: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
  • TechCrunch: ‘Outrageous,’ ‘reckless,’ ‘wow’: Here’s what politicians are saying about Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia

item.title: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler for $44B; Amazon snaps up Decart's AI tech for $7.5B
item.description:
Two blockbuster deals landed the same day. CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler, the zero-trust security provider, for $44 billion, betting that combining the two platforms will better equip enterprise customers to deploy AI agents securely. It's one of the largest cybersecurity acquisitions ever and a major consolidation play as security vendors race to own the AI-agent era.

Meanwhile, Amazon is acquiring Decart's AI optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal, timed as Amazon prepares to sell its Trainium AI chips more broadly. The move signals Amazon's intent to compete harder with Nvidia on AI hardware, pairing its own silicon with the software stack needed to make it run efficiently.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion
  • TechCrunch: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship; OpenAI brings GPT-6.2 Sol to Chat
item.description:
Anthropic launched Claude Ship, a new developer tool that lets AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes — aiming to remove the approval bottleneck now that AI writes so much code. As AI-generated code piles up, the review queue has become the choke point, and Anthropic is betting agents can be trusted with routine approvals.

OpenAI rolled out a version of GPT-6.2 Sol, its newest model, to the Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, tuned for everyday conversation less than a week after the model debuted in Work and Codex. And AWS launched Strands Decider v2, a family of five open decision models built on Google's Gemma 4, ranging from 2B to 31B parameters and released under the Apache 2.0 license.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
  • Techmeme: OpenAI rolls out a version of GPT-6.2 Sol that is "optimized for everyday conversation" to the Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users (Zac Hall/9to5Mac)
  • Techmeme: AWS debuts Strands Decider v2, a family of five open decision models based on Google's Gemma 4, ranging from 2B to 31B parameters, under the Apache 2.0 license (Frederic Lardinois/The New Stack)
  • Product Hunt — The best new products, every day: Claude Ship

item.title: Sierra doubles to a $30B valuation; Supertake raises $20M for AI investing
item.description:
Sierra, the enterprise customer-experience company co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round, doubling its valuation to $30 billion in just six months as demand for AI in customer service takes off. The round is a striking sign of how much capital is still flowing to proven AI application companies.

On the earlier-stage end, Supertake raised a $20 million seed led by Adjacent. The startup lets users express market predictions — “takes” on where things are headed — and uses AI agents to turn them into investment portfolios via Coinbase and Robinhood, so people can put money behind an idea without picking individual stocks.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
  • TechCrunch: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
  • Techmeme: Supertake, which uses AI agents to turn users' market predictions into investment portfolios via Coinbase and Robinhood, raised a $20M seed led by Adjacent (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)

item.title: Ex-OpenAI engineer accused of bugging exec meetings and recording trade secrets
item.description:
The case against former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, charged with bugging an executive conference room, is widening. U.S. prosecutors say he had dozens of OpenAI meeting recordings, many of them covering possible trade secrets. A court filing adds that he recorded a meeting with foreign government representatives and photographed a confidential term sheet with another company.

The filings paint a picture of sustained interception rather than a single incident, and the foreign-government angle raises the stakes considerably. The case is a reminder of the insider-threat risks at frontier AI labs, where a single engineer can have access to commercially and strategically sensitive material.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Filing: ex-OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan recorded a meeting with foreign government reps and photographed a confidential term sheet with another company (Emmy Martin/New York Times)
  • Techmeme: US prosecutors say the ex-OpenAI engineer charged with bugging an exec conference room had dozens of OpenAI meeting recordings, many on possible trade secrets (Madlin Mekelburg/Bloomberg)

item.title: Google pulled West Bank Maps updates after pressure; Meta drops net-zero goal
item.description:
Two of tech's biggest names walked back public commitments. Wired reports that a Google product manager spent years updating Maps to better serve Palestinians in the West Bank, accurately mapping Israeli checkpoints, but Google retracted key parts of the work after Israeli pressure. The episode raises pointed questions about how much political pressure shapes the world's most popular navigation app.

Meta walked back its 2030 net-zero goal in its 2026 sustainability report, a decision that could send ripples through the industry as other companies weigh their own climate pledges. And Figma and its CEO were sued by a current employee alleging sexual harassment and discrimination, including claims the company forced her to confront her harassers.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: a Google product manager spent years updating Maps to better serve Palestinians in the West Bank, but Google retracted key parts after Israeli pressure (Wired)
  • TechCrunch: Meta throws out its net-zero goal — its competitors should be furious
  • TechCrunch: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo; U.S. probes cyberattacks on up to 50 tankers
item.description:
OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect running Linux systems without a reboot while they roll out patches. The pitch is aimed at the window between a vulnerability being disclosed and a patch being applied — a gap AI has helped attackers exploit in seconds.

That threat was underscored by a separate report that the U.S. is investigating possible Iranian involvement in cyberattacks on up to 50 energy tankers, exploiting a Fortinet router flaw, with Russia also a possible culprit. As many as 50 ships carrying oil and other explosive substances are believed to have been attacked, making it one of the largest maritime cyber incidents reported to date.

Sources

  • Techmeme: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect running Linux systems without a reboot while they roll out patches (Mike Wheatley/SiliconANGLE)
  • Techmeme: Sources: the US is investigating Iran's possible role in cyberattacks on up to 50 energy tankers via a Fortinet router flaw; Russia is also a possible culprit (Wall Street Journal)

item.title: TPG and Corpay to take BILL Holdings private in a ~$6B deal
item.description:
Fintech firm BILL Holdings will be acquired by private equity group TPG, in partnership with Corpay, in a deal valued at around $6 billion. BILL's cloud-based software helps small and midsize businesses automate their financial operations — paying bills, invoicing, and managing cash flow.

It's one of the larger take-private deals of the year and a sign that private equity still sees value in public fintech names that the market has discounted. For BILL's customers, the pitch is continuity; for its shareholders, it's an exit at a price the public market wasn't offering.

Sources

  • Techmeme: TPG and Corpay agree to acquire and take private BILL Holdings, whose cloud-based software lets SMBs automate financial operations, in a deal valued at ~$6B

item.title: MBK Partners to take Wacom private in ~$860M deal, with Samsung participating
item.description:
South Korean private equity firm MBK Partners has agreed to take Japan's Wacom private in a deal valuing the digital pen technology company at about $860 million, with Samsung participating. Wacom supplies core pen technology for Samsung Electronics devices, among others.

The deal is a reminder of how much of the tech supply chain sits in quiet, specialized Japanese firms — Wacom's digitizers are in millions of devices, even though most users never know the name. Samsung's participation signals the strategic value of keeping that technology close.

Sources

  • Techmeme: South Korean PE firm MBK Partners agrees to take Japan's Wacom private, in a deal valuing the digital pen tech company at ~$860M, with Samsung participating

item.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
item.description:
Three significant backers — Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford — shared what gave them conviction to bet billions on Anthropic ahead of its IPO. The story is a window into how the biggest AI investments get made: not on current revenue, but on a belief about which lab's approach to building and governing frontier models will win.

With Anthropic's valuation climbing on the strength of Claude's enterprise adoption, these early bets are looking prescient — and the backers' reasoning offers a useful map of what sophisticated investors are actually underwriting in AI: model quality, enterprise trust, and a governance story that survives scrutiny.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO

item.title: Arva AI raises $20M Series A to build AI agents for banks' financial-crime teams
item.description:
Arva AI, which builds AI agents for banks' financial-crime compliance teams, has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Arthur Ventures. The company counts Wise among its customers.

Financial-crime compliance is a natural fit for AI agents: banks spend enormous sums on teams reviewing suspicious transactions, and the work is rules-heavy, document-heavy, and high-volume. Arva's bet is that agents can do much of that triage work — and a $20M raise from a respected fintech investor suggests the market agrees the opportunity is real.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Arva AI, which builds AI agents for banks' financial-crime compliance teams and counts Wise as a customer, raised a $20M Series A led by Arthur Ventures

item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
item.description:
To establish a speed limit on AI development, you first need to agree on how to measure speed. That's the crux of OpenAI's chief scientist's argument about limiting AI progress: any governance scheme depends on metrics that the field hasn't settled on — and that labs have incentives to game.

The piece lands in a week when METR warned that AI is improving faster than experts can reliably test it, and the Riemann hypothesis proof showed capabilities arriving decades early. The chief scientist's point is less about whether limits are desirable than whether they're even definable — and right now, the measuring tools are the missing piece.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

item.title: Alexandr Wang: the Riemann proof shows AI will surpass humans in every field
item.description:
Alexandr Wang says the Riemann hypothesis proof shows AI will surpass humans in every field — including AI research itself — and is calling for AI safety and alignment work to keep pace. "Superintelligence is arriving," he writes, reading the proof as evidence that the timeline for AI surpassing human experts has compressed dramatically.

Wang's reaction is the maximalist interpretation of the week's biggest AI story: not just a milestone in mathematics, but a signal that the frontier is moving faster than the institutions meant to govern it. Whether you buy the extrapolation or not, the proof has clearly become a Rorschach test for how people see AI's trajectory.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Alexandr Wang says the Riemann Hypothesis proof shows AI will surpass humans in every field, including AI research, and calls for AI safety and alignment

item.title: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash
item.description:
Journalist Paris Marx unpacks his new book "Hyperscale" and the argument that data centers — the physical infrastructure of the AI boom — have become the focal point of the backlash against Big Tech. The facilities consume enormous amounts of power and water, reshape local communities, and concentrate economic benefits in a few companies' hands.

The backlash is no longer abstract: it's about land, electricity bills, and water usage in specific towns. As AI demand keeps driving data center construction, the politics of where they get built and who pays for them is becoming one of the defining fights of the AI era.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Why data centers are at the center of the Big Tech backlash

item.title: DNI and AI czar Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director
item.description:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton — who also serves as the administration's AI czar — will take on a third role as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation, according to Axios sources.

The consolidation puts intelligence, AI policy, and cyber defense under one person, at least temporarily. It's a lot of hats for one official, and it underscores how intertwined AI and cybersecurity have become in Washington's thinking — the same person is now responsible for the nation's intelligence, its AI strategy, and its cyber defense.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation

item.title: The Jensen Huang scandal deepens as a chip-smuggling network comes into focus
item.description:
A Financial Times investigation reports that Alice Huang, the Chinese executive in a romantic relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, had ties to gaming firms, alleged Prince Group figures, and hundreds of shell companies in a network moving Nvidia chips to China. The findings add a serious national-security dimension to a scandal that began as a personal one.

Meanwhile, TechCrunch describes two very different pictures of Nvidia: a strong earnings report on one side, and tech executives loudly calling for Huang's return on the other. The fallout is even rippling into Silicon Valley dating life, with matchmakers telling Wired that newly wealthy tech workers increasingly fear romantic espionage, and at least one AI companion app now pitching "zero espionage" executive girlfriends. The scandal has moved well past gossip and is now shaping how the industry talks about trust, security, and leadership at its most valuable company.

Sources

  • Financial Times: Investigation: Alice Huang had ties to gaming firms, alleged Prince Group figures and hundreds of shell companies in a network moving Nvidia chips to China
  • TechCrunch: A tale of two Nvidias
  • Wired: Matchmakers say more tech workers fear romantic espionage after the Jensen Huang scandal; an AI companion app pitches "zero espionage" executive girlfriends

item.title: Amazon nears a $7.5B deal for AI startup Decart
item.description:
Amazon is nearing a $7.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Decart, according to the Financial Times, with talks at an advanced stage and a deal possibly coming together as soon as next week. The acquisition would help AWS compete with Nvidia in the race for computing power.

The deal would be one of the largest AI infrastructure bets yet by a cloud provider, and it signals that the compute arms race is shifting from buying chips to owning the companies that build the underlying technology. If it closes, it would put Amazon in a stronger position against rivals racing to secure the hardware and software stack behind the next wave of AI models.

Sources

  • Financial Times: Sources: Amazon is nearing a $7.5B deal to buy AI startup Decart; talks are at an advanced stage and a deal could come together as soon as next week

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots, calling AI surveillance an existential threat
item.description:
Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps, framing the move as a response to what it calls an existential threat from AI-powered surveillance. The messaging app, long a standard-bearer for private communication, is tightening one of the last gaps in its protections: content that can be captured off-screen.

The change underscores how AI tools that can read, transcribe, and analyze anything on a device are reshaping the threat model for privacy apps. For Signal, the calculation is that convenience matters less than closing a hole that increasingly capable AI systems could exploit at scale.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance

item.title: Researchers find AI routers routinely leak private data, even under "zero data retention" policies
item.description:
Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires, known as canary credentials, in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services and found that privacy protections were often broken. Requests routed through services like OpenRouter and Vercel leaked credentials and saw keys stolen, even when the services were operating under "zero data retention" policies that are supposed to prevent exactly that.

The findings are a warning for anyone sending sensitive data through AI intermediaries: the privacy promises in the fine print may not hold in practice. For developers and companies routing prompts through third-party AI gateways, the study suggests that data sent to these services should be treated as potentially exposed, regardless of what the policy page says.

Sources

  • Ars Technica: Researchers used canary credentials in requests to AI routers like OpenRouter and Vercel, even under "ZDR" policies, and saw "privacy" often broken, keys stolen

item.title: China's tech giants double AI spending while U.S. export rules widen
item.description:
China's biggest tech companies are set to double capital spending to $139 billion in 2026, according to Rhodium, but revenue from their AI labs still accounts for under 8% of that total. The New York Times reports the gap between spending and returns may matter more than chip curbs in determining whether China's AI push pays off, even as Silicon Valley rivals raise tens of billions in capital.

At the same time, tighter U.S. export controls introduced this week are reaching further than expected. Industry insiders tell Nikkei Asia the new rules affect a broader range of chips, including the system-on-a-chip parts used in consumer electronics, extending well beyond advanced AI chips. The combination paints a picture of an AI race where both sides are spending enormously, and where the constraints are as much financial and regulatory as technological.

Sources

  • New York Times: Rhodium: China's biggest tech companies are set to double capex to $139B in 2026 with AI lab revenue under 8% of it, a gap that may matter more than chip curbs
  • Nikkei Asia: Industry insiders say new US export rules affect a broader range of chips, including SoCs used in consumer electronics, extending beyond advanced AI chips

item.title: FBI investigates reported hack of its national crime database
item.description:
The FBI is reportedly investigating a hack of the National Crime Information Center, the bureau's database of criminal records. President Trump weighed in on the reported breach, calling it "not good."

Details remain thin, including what data may have been accessed and how the intrusion happened, but any compromise of the NCIC would be serious: the system underpins law enforcement lookups across the country. The incident is the latest in a run of high-profile breaches hitting government systems, and more specifics are likely to emerge as the investigation proceeds.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Trump says reported FBI database hack is ‘not good’

item.title: Microsoft will retire To Do in June 2027, with no replacement for personal users
item.description:
Microsoft plans to retire its To Do app on June 30, 2027, GeekWire reports. Work and school accounts will be offered a migration path to Microsoft Planner, but personal account users get no replacement, leaving longtime users of the app to find their own alternative.

The shutdown closes a long chapter: Microsoft acquired the popular task app Wunderlist in 2015, shut it down in 2020, and told loyal users To Do would be their new home. Now that home is closing too. With more than a year and a half of runway, users have time to migrate, but the move is a reminder that even widely used Microsoft apps are not guaranteed a future.

Sources

  • GeekWire: Microsoft plans to retire its To Do app on June 30, 2027, offering migration to Planner for work and school accounts, but no replacement for personal accounts

item.title: Nasdaq 100 suffers its worst week in six years as AI-spending fears grip Wall Street
item.description:
The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% on Friday, taking its loss for the week to 10.4% — its worst run in more than six years — amid fears of a slowdown in the AI investment boom. Shares in Anthropic and Nvidia tumbled as investors questioned whether the trillions being poured into AI infrastructure will ever pay off.

The timing is brutal for Anthropic, which completed the largest IPO in history just a day earlier. The broader question now facing the market is whether the AI trade has been a rational bet on a real transformation or a bubble built on circular spending: chipmakers selling to labs, labs renting from cloud providers, and everyone pointing at everyone else's revenue. This week, the market started asking for proof.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% on Friday, taking its loss for the week to 10.4%, its worst run in more than six years, amid fears of a slowdown in the AI investment boom (Financial Times)

item.title: Behind Jensen Huang's exit: a management style reportedly built on fear, and a subpoena from California
item.description:
The fallout from Jensen Huang's ouster at Nvidia keeps widening. New reporting questions a management style reportedly built on fear — and Elon Musk's claim that Nvidia's employees "love" the ousted CEO may have been overstating it. Meanwhile, California Attorney General Rob Bonta has subpoenaed Nvidia over worries about Huang's ties with China, saying the conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO "raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors."

Nvidia was, until recently, the unquestioned center of the AI boom. Now it faces a leadership vacuum, a regulatory probe, and a stock slide — all at once. How the company navigates the next few months will shape not just Nvidia but the whole AI hardware market.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Behind Jensen Huang’s exit, questions about a management style reportedly built on fear
  • TechCrunch: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over worries about Huang’s ties with China

item.title: SoftBank's Son explored a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix
item.description:
SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son recently approached Wall Street institutions about financing a possible trillion-dollar buyout of memory chip giant SK Hynix, according to The Information. SoftBank says the deal is "no longer under active consideration."

A trillion dollars would be the largest acquisition in history by a wide margin, and the fact that it got as far as financing conversations says a lot about the scale of ambition in the AI memory market. SK Hynix is the dominant supplier of high-bandwidth memory — the chips that feed AI accelerators — and whoever controls it controls a chokepoint in the AI supply chain. The deal may be dead, but the strategic logic behind it isn't going away.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: Masayoshi Son recently explored a possible $1T buyout of SK Hynix; SoftBank says the deal is "no longer under active consideration" (The Information)

item.title: Oracle says it has secured funding for its OpenAI infrastructure contract
item.description:
Oracle says it has secured all the funding it needs to fulfill its infrastructure contract with OpenAI, and that "any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options." With its final capital raise earlier this month, Oracle says it became the first hyperscaler fully funded for this investment cycle.

The statement is aimed squarely at skeptics who have questioned whether Oracle — and the AI infrastructure buildout more broadly — can actually pay for itself. Oracle's financing, including vendor financing outlined at its Investor Day, has been under scrutiny as the market turns skeptical about AI spending. Whether the reassurance lands will depend on whether investors believe the demand is real or just another round of circular AI deals.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Oracle says it has secured funding for its infrastructure contract with OpenAI and "any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options" (@oracle)

item.title: Databricks and Cognition chase sky-high valuations in a funding frenzy
item.description:
Two of the hottest AI companies are raising again at sharply higher valuations. Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars at around a $225 billion valuation, up nearly 20% from its $190 billion round in August. Cognition, the AI coding startup, is considering raising $2 billion or more at a $75 billion valuation — after already raising over $3 billion in 2026, including $2 billion at $48 billion in September.

The pace is dizzying: Cognition's valuation has risen by more than half in two months. Both raises come in the same week the public markets punished AI stocks, which makes the private-market enthusiasm either a sign of durable confidence or a lagging indicator. Either way, the money keeps flowing.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars at a ~$225B valuation, after closing a $5B round at a $190B valuation in August (Wall Street Journal)
  • Techmeme: Sources: Cognition is considering raising $2B or more at a $75B valuation, after raising over $3B in 2026 so far, including $2B at a $48B valuation in September (Bloomberg)

item.title: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68 billion — a third of what Intuit paid
item.description:
Bending Spoons has agreed to buy Mailchimp for $3.68 billion. Intuit acquired the email marketing company in 2021 for roughly $12 billion, so Bending Spoons is getting it for less than a third of that price.

The deal is a vivid marker of how the last cycle's valuations have deflated — and of Bending Spoons' strategy of buying mature software businesses and running them efficiently. Mailchimp remains a huge product with millions of small-business customers; the question is whether its new owner can revive growth that stalled under Intuit, or simply harvest a durable cash cow.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp for $3.68B

item.title: Hackers breached federal systems at the FBI and USDA as the national cyber director steps down
item.description:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its NCIC database — the nationwide system law enforcement uses to share information on warrants and background checks — according to CNN. Separately, hackers breached the Agriculture Department's system that facilitates payments to farmers this week, the agency told employees on Thursday.

The breaches come as the US national cyber director is stepping down, and against a backdrop of unexplained outages at the FAA, Microsoft, Apple, Chase, and the NSA this week. Officials insist the outages weren't a coordinated attack, but two federal breaches in one week is hard to dismiss. The NCIC breach is especially sensitive: it's the database every police department in the country relies on.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its NCIC database, which is used by law enforcement to share info on warrants and background checks (CNN)
  • Techmeme: Sources: hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture's system that facilitates payments to farmers this week (NBC News)
  • TechCrunch: The US national cyber director is stepping down

item.title: Wonder is exploring a sale of Grubhub, two years after buying it for $650 million
item.description:
Wonder is exploring a sale of Grubhub, which it bought in 2024 for $650 million, according to the Wall Street Journal. Bankers have been in contact with Walmart, Target, Kroger, and other retailers about a potential purchase.

The short holding period tells its own story: Wonder bought Grubhub as part of a bet on combining food delivery with its meal-kit business, and the fit apparently hasn't materialized. A sale to a big retailer would make strategic sense — Walmart and Target both want a food-delivery arm — but it would also mark Grubhub's third ownership change in a decade.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: Wonder is exploring a sale of Grubhub, which it bought in 2024 for $650M; bankers have been in contact with Walmart, Target, Kroger and other retailers (Wall Street Journal)

item.title: Cursor considers phasing out Chinese AI models over 'geopolitical risk'
item.description:
Cursor has told lawmakers it is considering phasing out Chinese open-weight AI models due to "geopolitical risk." The irony: Cursor's Composer 2 was built on Kimi K2.5, a Chinese model from Moonshot AI.

The disclosure shows how quickly geopolitics is reshaping AI tooling. Open-weight Chinese models have become genuinely competitive — good enough to power flagship products from American companies — and that dependence is now a political liability. If Cursor drops them, it's a meaningful vote of no confidence in the open-weight ecosystem's most important contributor, and a sign that the AI supply chain is splitting along national lines.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Cursor tells lawmakers it is considering phasing out Chinese open-weight AI models due to "geopolitical risk"; Cursor's Composer 2 was built on Kimi K2.5 (CNBC)

item.title: Anthropic's record IPO pops, then pulls back — and makes its backers billions
item.description:
Anthropic went public in the largest IPO in history, pricing at $83 a share and raising roughly $107 billion, then opened on Nasdaq at $111 — up 33% — before falling about 5% in after-hours trading as a broad selloff cooled the debut-day euphoria. The listing was a windfall machine: the seven founders each pocketed about $280 million, Iconiq's $6 billion-plus bet is now worth roughly $32 billion, and Menlo's $1 billion-plus stake is worth $20 billion-plus. The IPO could also deliver up to $156 billion to charity through the company's Public Benefit Foundation and a company match.

The bigger question is whether the business can support the valuation. Anthropic faces enormous compute commitments, and much of its financing runs through its biggest infrastructure partners, Amazon and Google, who would keep profiting even if Anthropic loses its lead. Rival Fireworks AI argued the same day that most companies can skip the pricey frontier models and use cheaper open models instead. CEO Dario Amodei used the opening-bell moment to recommit to pacing AI development regardless of business or political pressure.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Anthropic hits Nasdaq exchanges at $111, 33% above IPO price
  • Techmeme: Anthropic fell ~5% in after-hours trading on its debut day, following a record $107.3B IPO (Bloomberg)

  • Techmeme: Source: Iconiq invested more than $6B in Anthropic; its estimated 1.8% stake was worth ~$31.8B at Thursday's close, a 430%+ return on investment (Richard Nieva/Forbes)
  • Techmeme: Sources: Menlo invested $1B+ for a ~1.5% Anthropic stake, worth $20B+ at a $1.5T valuation; Lightspeed, the top financial investor, invested $3B+ and holds 2%+ (Krystal Hu/Reuters)
  • TechCrunch: Anthropic’s IPO could deliver $156B to charity
  • TechCrunch: Anthropic’s IPO puts AI’s circular financing boom to the test
  • TechCrunch: Anthropic rival says companies can (mostly) skip the pricey models
  • TechCrunch: At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development

item.title: The Jensen Huang scandal deepens: California subpoenas Nvidia over China chips
item.description:
The fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia widened on Thursday. California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to the chipmaker, probing whether Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips and whether Nvidia misled investors. The subpoena follows reports of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, a sequence TechCrunch laid out in a full timeline of how the scandal unfolded.

Separately, documents obtained by CNBC show that as of May 2026, the Commerce Department's export-control arm had approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies — including entities on the Pentagon's list of Chinese military-linked firms. The two threads together put Nvidia at the center of the U.S.-China AI race in a way no earnings report ever could, and the investigation is still in its early stages, with the legal and national-security consequences far from settled.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
  • Techmeme: California's AG subpoenas Nvidia to investigate whether Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China getting advanced chips, and whether Nvidia misled investors (Katie Nicora/CBS News)
  • Techmeme: Docs: as of May 2026, the US Commerce Dept. approved sales of 879K+ AI chips to Chinese companies, including entities on the DOD's Chinese military-linked list (CNBC)

item.title: Nvidia eyes a $500M-plus deal for diffusion-model startup Inception
item.description:
Even amid the Huang scandal, Nvidia is pushing ahead on the deal front: the company is in advanced talks to acquire Inception, a two-year-old startup building diffusion-based large language models, for more than $500 million plus earnouts. Diffusion models aim to generate text faster than the standard autoregressive approach by refining output in parallel rather than token by token.

Notably, the talks began before Huang's resignation, suggesting the acquisition is a strategic technology bet rather than a reaction to the turmoil. If it closes, it would give Nvidia a foothold in a fundamentally different model architecture at a moment when inference speed is becoming a key competitive battleground.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire diffusion LLM developer Inception for $500M+ plus earnouts; talks began before Jensen Huang's resignation (The Information)

item.title: AI agents are coming for your Mac — from both Apple and Google
item.description:
The race to build an AI agent that operates your computer directly hit the Mac from both sides on Thursday. Google shipped an update giving Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you — organizing files, filling out forms, and carrying out multistep workflows on the desktop. Meanwhile, Apple appears to be developing its own Mac agent, one that could compete with the likes of Meta Muse, Claude, and OpenAI's tools.

The timing matters: whoever controls the agent layer on the desktop controls the next interface for getting work done. Google has moved first with a shipping product, while Apple's effort is still reportedly in development. The open question is how much autonomy users will trust these agents with — and how the platforms will sandbox them so an agent that can click anything doesn't do something you regret.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
  • TechCrunch: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you

item.title: Meta's Muse is mixing up users' conversations — and possibly exposing private data
item.description:
Meta's AI agent Muse has a serious identity problem. According to a new report, the agent has been mixing up conversations between users — surfacing childcare requests they never made, career advice they never asked for, product orders they never placed, and even bank account balances that didn't belong to them. Employees described the cross-contamination as a privacy failure, not a minor glitch, since the leaked material can include financial details.

The report lands just as Meta is preparing to push Muse deeper into daily life: its upcoming Muse Charm wearable is reportedly priced around $300, and Meta has not denied the reporting, saying only that it will have more to share soon. The contrast is stark — a company asking users to wear its agent everywhere while that agent is reportedly confusing one person's life with another's.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Meta’s AI agent Muse is mixing up conversations and could be exposing private data, report says
  • TechCrunch: Meta’s new Muse Charm device may cost $300

item.title: A wave of tech outages — and the firing of the national cyber director
item.description:
The recent string of outages hitting airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity tools may not be a coincidence. Cybersecurity experts told TechCrunch there's likely something deeper going on — and one theory gaining traction is that the failures have a common thread in the AI-agent era, evoking Y2K-style systemic fragility rather than isolated bugs.

The political fallout arrived fast: White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross was fired, with the president fully supporting the decision, days after the wave of outages. Whether the outages share a single cause or are just a cluster of unrelated failures is still unclear, but the firing signals the administration treats them as a serious national cybersecurity problem rather than routine downtime.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style
  • Techmeme: Source: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was "fired" from his role; the president "fully supported" the firing days after a wave of tech-related outages (Courtney Rozen/Reuters)

item.title: UK government forced to disclose its secret Apple backdoor order
item.description:
A UK tribunal has forced the government to disclose its secret order demanding Apple build a backdoor into its encrypted services, rejecting London's claim that disclosure would damage national security. The order — issued under the Investigatory Powers Act and long kept under a veil of secrecy — is now coming into the open, at least in part.

The ruling is a significant win for transparency advocates and for Apple, which has resisted government demands to weaken encryption. It also sets a precedent: governments can no longer assume these surveillance orders will stay hidden from public scrutiny. The full contents of the order and its practical consequences for UK users' encrypted data remain to be seen.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order

item.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion
item.description:
Anthropic has priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 a share, above its projected range, in a debut that reportedly values the AI lab at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

That figure would make it one of the largest public listings in tech history and a defining test of investor appetite for frontier AI companies, arriving at a moment when the industry is simultaneously booming and under intense scrutiny over safety, regulation, and the economics of model building. How the stock trades in its first days will set a benchmark for every other AI company weighing a public debut.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range

item.title: Silicon Valley rallies around ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
item.description:
The fallout from Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia dominated the day. Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and the industry's biggest names lined up to defend him. Elon Musk said ousting Huang was like "kicking Michael Jordan off your team" and that he doesn't believe Huang is disloyal to the United States. Sam Altman said it's "hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen." Anduril's Palmer Luckey went further, arguing China is "thrilled to have Jensen out," that removing him "makes America weaker," and that Huang should be reinstated.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella struck a steadier note, expressing confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress. Meanwhile Nvidia added to the intrigue by announcing it won't file its routine quarterly 10-Q for weeks — a surprise one Wall Street analyst has now reportedly explained. The episode leaves the world's most important chipmaker in an unusually unsettled position, with its founder's exit, a leadership transition, and delayed financial filings all landing at once.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like ‘kicking Michael Jordan off your team’
  • TechCrunch: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says it’s ‘hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen’
  • TechCrunch: Palmer Luckey thinks China is ‘thrilled to have Jensen out,’ so he wants the ousted Nvidia CEO reinstated
  • TechCrunch: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit
  • TechCrunch: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report

item.title: Nadella explains why Microsoft asked 60,000 employees to quit
item.description:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why the company offered buyouts to 60,000 employees in October — effectively urging them to leave voluntarily rather than cutting the workforce through another massive layoff. The short answer, he said, is AI, though not in the way most people might expect.

The framing matters: Microsoft is choosing a softer, voluntary route to reshape its workforce as AI changes what the company needs from its people, rather than repeating the blunt layoff rounds that have defined the industry's recent cost-cutting. How the buyout program plays out — and whether other giants follow the same playbook — will be a signal for how tech's AI transition treats its workforce.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit

item.title: Nadella: AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web — and much of our infrastructure is 'unpatchable'
item.description:
Satya Nadella used his appearance to sketch how AI agents could upend the internet's business model, arguing they will disrupt advertising-driven economics and force companies like Amazon to rethink how they compete for customers. If agents, rather than people browsing and clicking ads, become the ones making purchasing decisions, the web's dominant revenue engine has to change.

On security, Nadella was blunt: lots of critical infrastructure is "unpatchable," even as he downplayed the recent Outlook outage. He acknowledged AI is creating both opportunities and new challenges for securing the connected world. Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey sounded the sharper alarm, warning that AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses and that outdated technology is leaving systems exposed: "It's time to start running."

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web
  • TechCrunch: Amidst fears of AI cyberattacks, Satya Nadella says lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’
  • TechCrunch: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’

item.title: Meta employees warn Muse may be mixing up conversations between accounts
item.description:
Internal posts show Meta employees raising concerns that Muse — Meta's AI assistant, downloaded more than 10 million times — could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users' private data. Staff flagged unbidden actions by the assistant, raising the prospect that one user's private information could surface in another's session.

The concern lands awkwardly for Meta, which expects Muse to generate billions in revenue. A cross-account data leak would be a serious trust problem for a product designed to sit inside people's daily lives and handle their personal information — and the fact that the warnings are coming from inside the company makes them harder to dismiss.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Internal posts show Meta employees raising concerns that Muse could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users' private data (Katie Paul/Reuters)

item.title: Arizona opens criminal investigation into AI agents at banks — as banks tell customers they're on their own
item.description:
Arizona has opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," according to the state's attorney general. The investigation puts the fast-growing world of autonomous AI agents — software that can act on a user's behalf, including moving money — squarely in regulators' sights.

At the same time, banks are drawing their own line. Citi is the latest major financial institution to say customers who use personal finance AI agents are on their own, even if they get hacked. The two developments together sketch an emerging fault line: agents are gaining real financial power, but neither the companies building them nor the banks holding the money want to own what happens when things go wrong.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Arizona's AG opens a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents" (David Thomas/Reuters)
  • TechCrunch: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked

item.title: Commerce official reportedly pressured staff to fast-track Nvidia H200 sales to China
item.description:
Jeffrey Kessler, the official overseeing the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security, has reportedly pressured staff to expedite Nvidia H200 chip sales to China despite red flags raised by other departments. The H200 is a powerful AI accelerator, and its export to China sits at the center of the U.S. government's effort to limit Beijing's access to advanced AI hardware.

If the account holds, it suggests tension inside the administration over how strictly those export controls are enforced — with the official in charge of the bureau pushing approvals through over objections from elsewhere in government. For Nvidia, the outcome determines access to one of its largest markets; for Washington, it tests whether the chip-control regime is holding.

Sources

  • Techmeme: Sources: Jeffrey Kessler, who oversees the Commerce Dept.'s BIS, pressured staff to expedite Nvidia H200 China sales despite red flags from other departments (The Information)

item.title: Funding and deals: Payhawk hits a $2B valuation, MegaRobo raises ~$200M, Kraken's parent buys Tribe Capital
item.description:
It was a busy day for startup money. Spend management platform Payhawk announced a $280 million raise at a $2 billion valuation. Founded in 2018, the company helps enterprises track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents — a sign that AI-native fintech is still commanding premium valuations.

Beijing-based MegaRobo, which uses robotics and AI to automate lab work for biotech research, raised nearly $200 million from investors including Oman's sovereign wealth fund. The company became a unicorn after raising $300 million in 2022. And in crypto, Kraken parent Payward agreed to buy Tribe Capital, the venture firm formerly led by Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi, which manages $2.7 billion in assets — a deal that tightens the ties between a major exchange and the VC world.

  • TechCrunch: Spend management platform Payhawk announces $280M raise, 2B valuation

  • Techmeme: Kraken parent company Payward agrees to buy Tribe Capital, the VC firm formerly led by Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi; Tribe Capital has $2.7B in assets (CoinDesk)

item.title: Nvidia board split over bringing Jensen Huang back
item.description:
Nvidia says it has no plans to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, a week after the founder resigned — but the question is far from settled. Huang said in his first public statement since stepping down that he would be "honored" to return, and Semafor reports a faction of board members is pushing for exactly that, despite board chair Harvey Jones publicly stating there are no reinstatement plans.

The split leaves Nvidia's leadership in limbo at the worst possible moment: the company is the center of the AI buildout, and investors are now weighing whether the board can hold its line against both Huang's willingness and internal pressure. For now the official position is no return — but the public disagreement means the story is still live.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Nvidia says it doesn’t plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO
  • Techmeme: Sources: a faction of Nvidia board members is pushing for Jensen Huang's return despite Chair Harvey Jones stating the board has no plans to reinstate Huang (Semafor)
  • TechCrunch: Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ if allowed to return as Nvidia CEO

item.title: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia as fallout widens
item.description:
The SEC is reportedly opening a probe into Nvidia following Huang's departure, according to the Wall Street Journal — Huang admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and regulators are now circling the company he built. Separately, The Information reports that former Nvidia sales chief Jay Puri, who controlled chip sales to major customers including Supermicro, is married to a former Supermicro executive, raising conflict-of-interest questions about how chip allocations were handled.

Neither report yet spells out specific charges, but together they widen the scandal from a CEO's personal conduct into questions about governance and sales practices. For a company whose chips power the AI boom, even the perception of compromised allocation decisions could draw sustained scrutiny.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia amid Huang exit
  • Techmeme: Sources: ex-Nvidia executive Jay Puri, who oversaw clients like Alice Huang, controlled chip sales to Supermicro; Puri is married to an ex-Supermicro executive (The Information)

item.title: Nvidia promises soaring revenue — but exits China and its startup bets wobble
item.description:
Despite the turmoil, Nvidia projected its streak of record-breaking revenue will continue — the demand for its chips hasn't blinked. But the new leadership is already redrawing strategy: interim CEO says the company is done selling chips to China, a major market exit with an unclear price tag.

Two other pillars of Huang's era are now uncertain. Nvidia's private startup investments have nearly tripled in nine months to $65 billion, fueled by Huang's aggressive dealmaking — but future deals are in doubt without him. The one continuity: the interim CEO reaffirmed Nvidia's open-source AI strategy and its plans to acquire Hugging Face. The business is strong; the empire Huang built around it is being renegotiated.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
  • TechCrunch: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
  • TechCrunch: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
  • TechCrunch: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit

item.title: Amazon and Google will own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO
item.description:
Amazon will own just under 15% of Anthropic after its IPO, with an option to go much higher, and Google holds nearly 14% — together, the two cloud giants will control almost 30% of one of the leading AI labs. The concentration raises obvious questions about how independent Anthropic can remain when its biggest shareholders are also its biggest infrastructure providers and rivals.

The IPO is also minting a historic fortune for insiders. A Bloomberg analysis finds San Francisco-based AI startup insiders hold a combined $1.2 trillion in equity, and at Anthropic's IPO midpoint the average employee's stake is worth about $72 million. It's a world-historical jackpot for a small circle — and a vivid measure of how much of the AI boom's value has accrued to employees of a handful of firms.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO
  • Techmeme: Analysis: San Francisco-based AI startup insiders hold a combined $1.2T in equity; at Anthropic's IPO midpoint, the average employee's equity is valued at $72M (Bloomberg)

item.title: Outage week: officials say no attack, blame a patch rush — as Apple goes down too
item.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is "zero evidence" linking the recent FAA ground stop, Microsoft outage, and bank service failures, and that the US is not "under systemic attack." A different explanation emerged from Congress: Wall Street executives and the NSA told lawmakers the outages stemmed from systems overwhelmed by a rush to patch vulnerabilities found by AI models — in other words, the fixes themselves broke things.

The failures kept coming: Apple services including iCloud, the App Store, and Apple Music were hit by an outage of unconfirmed cause, and public distrust is growing as travel and banking keep faltering. Google, notably, took the unusual step of publicly announcing that Gmail is working fine. The emerging picture is less a coordinated attack than fragile infrastructure buckling under its own maintenance.

Sources

item.title: Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order
item.description:
Waymo has suspended freeway rides nationwide after the California DMV ordered it to stop, saying its freeway operations pose an "imminent hazard to public safety." The restrictions stay in place until Waymo can demonstrate "effective corrective actions" addressing the deficiencies the DMV identified.

The nationwide scope is the striking part: a California order has halted freeway service across all of Waymo's markets, not just in the state. For the robotaxi leader, which has been steadily expanding freeway driving as a key capability, this is a significant operational setback — and a reminder that regulators can still pull the plug on its most advanced deployments.

Sources

  • TechCrunch: Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order

item.title: Huawei criminal trial heads to the jury after two months of testimony
item.description:
After two months of testimony, the US criminal trial against Huawei — accused of bank fraud and trade secret theft — is set to begin jury deliberations on Wednesday. In closing arguments, a defense lawyer argued prosecutors had put a "sinister spin" on the Chinese tech company's conduct.

The case is one of the most consequential US prosecutions of a foreign tech company ever brought, with implications for Huawei's global business and for US-China tech tensions. A verdict could land within days, and either outcome will be closely watched in Washington and Beijing.

Sources

  • Techmeme: After two months of testimony, the US criminal trial against Huawei, accused of bank fraud and trade secret theft, is set to begin jury deliberations Wednesday (Karen Freifeld/Reuters)

item.title: Model ML raises $250M; LanceDB lands $57.5M Series B
item.description:
Model ML raised $250 million to automate investment banking grunt work, with agents that understand the full context of bankers' deals and automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect the analysis. It's one of the largest AI-application rounds of the year, betting that white-collar deal work is next in line for automation.

LanceDB raised a $57.5 million Series B led by Bessemer and Innovation Endeavors for its multimodal lakehouse built on the open Lance format, designed to speed up AI training. Together, the two rounds show capital still flowing heavily to AI — both the infrastructure underneath it and the knowledge-work applications on top.

Sources

  • Techmeme: LanceDB, which makes a multimodal lakehouse for AI training, built on the open format Lance, raised a $57.5M Series B led by Bessemer and Innovation Endeavors (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
